# Figure 1 — One position table, two carriers, two very different stories

> **Tier: T2 — provenance.** Supporting record: preregistrations, decision logs, correction ledgers, audits.

**Generated by** `scripts/splicebert/make_fig1_summary.py` from `results/phase-lattice/fig_report_data.json`.

SpliceBERT's position-embedding table carries two learned oscillators. They are not two aspects
of one code: their carrier planes are **orthogonal** in embedding space (subspace overlap
**0.0003**, against **0.99** for a bin and its own sidebands). The figure draws them apart for
that reason, and only that reason.

## The period-3 branch (blue) — a circuit with a job

The period-3 carrier feeds six early-layer comb heads, which feed **L2H15** (the acceptor
addresser), which feeds **L3H1** (the reader). The donor arrives at L3H1 as *content*; the
acceptor is found by *address*. Deleting the carrier collapses donor–acceptor coupling from
**0.946 to 0.026**, and the damage is specific to coding sequence — exons lose **0.159 nats**,
introns **0.042**. Restoring L2H15 alone recovers **36.3%** of the lost coupling, against a
best-of-24 random single head of 4.2%.

## The ≈10.63 branch (orange) — a circuit whose purpose is unknown

The ≈10.63 carrier is read through the softmax by **eight heads** that pass every control: the
pattern collapses when the carrier is deleted (40–44% retained), survives deletion of a
reciprocal band (89–97%) and of a low-leak band (~100%), and survives **content shuffling**
(93–107%) — which is what a *positional* comb must do, and what a content artefact cannot.

**The branch stops there.** No downstream effect has been demonstrated. There is no arrow from
it to splicing, to chromatin, or to translation, and the figure must not be read as implying
one. What these eight heads *do* with the carrier is the open question this report ends on.

## A note on checkpoints

The two branches were measured in different checkpoints of the same training lineage, and the
figure says so in its footer. The period-3 circuit is measured in **SpliceBERT.1024nt** (final,
multi-species). The Level-A attention circuit is measured in **SpliceBERT.510nt** (stage-1,
multi-species) — because establishing it required a matched contrast against
**SpliceBERT-human.510nt**, its twin, which differs *only* in training data. That contrast is
Figure 4A, and it is the reason the null in the human-only model can be believed.

## What is deliberately not claimed

- 10.63 is called a **carrier**, never a *phase*. The plane is a near-perfect circle
  (circularity 0.992); it contains every phase. A head *selects* a phase from it through its
  QK bilinear form. See Figure 2B.
- The coupling collapse quoted here (0.946 → 0.026) is from the **dose** run (n = 256). The
  mediation run (n = 160, Figure 3D) has its own baseline, 0.943 → 0.034, and its rescue
  percentages are of *that* lost coupling. The two are different experiments and are not mixed.
